title: [spec-gap][R-02-063] C persist-mode trust store refuses admission (-ENOSPC) instead of MUST LRU-evict on overflow (spec 02 4.2)
description: Req R-02-063 (spec/02-physical-link.md 4.2 rule 6): trust store MUST be bounded to at most 256 entries; on overflow implementations MUST evict the least-recently-verified binding (LRU by last-verified). DIVERGENT: without CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_REPLAY_PERSIST, C LRU-evicts (lichen_l2_peer.c:348-374 via peer_find_oldest_locked :63-83); WITH persist mode it returns -ENOSPC and refuses admission (lichen_l2_peer.c:341-347, rationale 'Durable replay history is trust lineage'). Rust bound 64 peers LRU by last_access (link_layer.rs:553-560, :991-1011); Python MAX_ENTRIES=64 OrderedDict LRU (link_layer.py:1657, :1696-1697); C Kconfig default 16 range 4-64 (link/Kconfig:28-35). All bounds are < 256 (satisfies 'at most 256' but no test asserts the literal ceiling). The persist-mode refuse-admission behavior is a deliberate security posture that contradicts the MUST-evict clause — needs either an implementation change or an adjudicated spec carve-out (trust-lineage protection vs MUST-evict). Suggested placement: decide via spec amendment (mark) or add LRU eviction to C persist mode; related: 2dd7 (announce trust brick), a459 (durable SCHC floors exhaust TOFU capacity).
